messages:
maya: Quick sync — we're proposing a coordinated kernel (5.15.0-rcX) + NVIDIA driver (535.86) + GPU firmware (v1.2.4) bump across g4/g5 pools in us-west-2 to address persistent Xid and ECC escalations. Goal: reduce Xid rate by >=60% in a 7-day window. Scheduling: prefer low-traffic window Wed 02:00-06:00. Thoughts?

raj: Do we have concrete gating metrics and canary size? also need to validate inference latency/regressions (p50/p95) and KV cache behavior.

leah: Proposed pipeline: 5% canary (~30 hosts) -> 20% ramp -> fleet-wide. Canary checks: per-host Xid/sec, ECC corrected/sec, gpu_reboot_rate, p95 inference latency, and nvlink errors. Gate if Xid/sec doesn't drop by >=50% or p95 increases >5%. Rollback on any host-level kernel oops.

sam: +1 on gating. For smoke tests we should run the synthetic inference harness with 20k tokens/host for 6 hours and also run long-tail sequence workloads (2k tokens). Capture traces for kernel oops and nv-host logs.

maya: Canary automation snippet (what we'll run on each canary host):

```
# cordon, drain, upgrade, reboot, sanity
fleetctl cordon $NODE
fleetctl drain $NODE --grace=300
ssh $NODE "sudo apt-get install linux-image-5.15.0-rcX -y && sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-535 -y && sudo reboot"
# after reboot
ssh $NODE "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,firmware_version --format=csv"
# smoke harness
ssh $NODE "/opt/smoke/run_inference_smoke --tokens 20000 --trace /tmp/trace.json"
```

maria: (reaction) :thumbsup:  // note: maria isn't in participants list, stray emoji from a different thread

leah: Telemetry checks (implemented in canary job):
- pre/post Xid/sec (aggregated 1h)
- ECC corrected/sec and uncorrected events
- host kernel oops and module taints
- p50/p95 latency, cpu usage, and memory pressure
- nv_peer_mem/fatal errors

maya: Example gating rules (pseudo):
- if post.Xid_per_sec <= pre.Xid_per_sec * 0.5 and p95_latency_change <= 1.05 => pass
- if host_oops_count > 0 or uncorrected_ECC > 0 => fail and rollback host
- rollback command: `fleetctl uncordon $NODE` + reimage to last-good AMI

infra-bot: Canary batch 1 finished on 30 hosts (canary-2026-03-18-01). Telemetry summary: Xid/sec median drop 68%, ECC_corrected stable, gpu_reboot_rate reduced 40%, p95 latency +1.2%. No kernel oops observed. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/canary-2026-03-18-01 

devops: Important: exclude Dedicated and Reserved pools from automatic ramp. us-west-2a has two reserved racks with pinned capacity — we should target compute pool only. Also estimate cost of drain-induced lost throughput ~0.9 node-equivalent/day during ramp -> ~$2.1k for a 7-day rollout window.

raj: Good results from infra-bot. Next questions: region rollout order and fallback model. If capacity scarce, can we route traffic to us-east-1 or spin transient spot GPUs in a different AZ? Also, we need a soft-fallback to the previous driver & firmware version for customer-critical routes.

maya: Plan: run canary in us-west-2, then us-east-1, then eu-west-1. Ramp pause points at 20% and 60% with manual approval. Fallback implemented via image-based reimage to last-good AMI. Also adding routing policy: route high-priority customer traffic to nodes tagged `no-upgrade` during global ramp.

sam: I'll prepare the smoke harness dashboards and the automated approval PR. Can we add a per-model cost telemetry check so Optimize team knows the unit-cost delta before/after?

leah: Add a regression alert that triggers if p95 latency increases >3% for any top-5 models for >30m. That should catch subtle perf regressions.

maya: OK — I'll schedule the first canary for Wed 02:00 PST and open the rollout PR with gates, rollback steps, and the cost estimate. Will ping infra channel when PR is ready. Thanks all. :rocket:
